mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as a consistent trend without triggering conditions.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness that triggers equity market risk-off behavior, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days when the threshold is crossed.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of weak GDP growth (GDPC1 < 11000) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 198) creates a stagflationary environment that triggers equity market sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when GDPC1 < 11000 AND CPIAUCSL > 198 (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY inflation > 2.0%), rate hikes increase the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% AND CPIAUCSL (YoY) > 2.0% (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained payroll employment level above 130,000 reflects robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as a consistent trend.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130,000 (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained housing starts level above 2000 indicates strong consumer demand for housing, a leading indicator of economic expansion that produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST > 2000 (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained GDP growth level above 11000 indicates strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when GDPC1 > 11000 (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production level above 115 reflects strong manufacturing output, a leading indicator of economic health that produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when INDPRO > 115 (as of decision date), or Rank IC over 2010-2011 < 0.05.
